saints.name: St. Lydia
saints.title: Disciple of St. Paul
saints.shortBlurb: A seller of purple cloth at Philippi who became the first recorded convert to Christ in Europe…
biography: Paul, called by a vision into Macedonia, came to Philippi, a Roman colony, and on the Sabbath sought a place of prayer by the river outside the gate, where certain women gathered. Among them was Lydia, a seller of purple cloth from Thyatira in Asia Minor, a Gentile 'worshipper of God' drawn to the Jewish faith.

As Paul spoke, Acts records, 'the Lord opened her heart' to heed his words, and she was baptized with her whole household, the first recorded converts to Christ on European soil. She at once pressed hospitality on the apostles: 'If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come to my house and stay.'

When Paul and Silas were released from the Philippian prison, it was to Lydia's house that they returned to encourage the brethren. Because her trade was the costly purple dye for which Thyatira was famed, she is honoured as patroness of dyers; the Roman Martyrology keeps her memory on 3 August.
saints.knownFor: Being the first convert to Christianity in Europe.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 3 August
